crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Satellite Imagery
children.blurb: Satellite imagery as alternative data means using pictures of the Earth taken from orbit to answer questions that financial and economic analysts care about.

children.name: Card Transaction Data
children.blurb: Card transaction data covers the records generated when a payment card is used, including the merchant, the amount, the timestamp and a category code, with the cardholder identity removed or masked.

children.name: Sensor and Shipping Data
children.blurb: Sensor and shipping data covers the physical signals that track goods and vessels as they move: automatic identification system (AIS) broadcasts from ships, port call records, container and terminal throughput, satellite imagery of vessels and storage tanks, and telemetry from trucks, rail and warehouse equipment.

children.name: Mobile Location Data
children.blurb: Mobile location data is the record of where a phone has been, inferred from signals such as GPS, Wi-Fi connections and cell tower handoffs.

children.name: Web Data Collection
children.blurb: Web data collection is the practice of gathering information from public websites and web services at scale, usually by automated means, to build datasets that feed research, analytics and machine learning.

sections.body: Alternative data means information generated as a byproduct of ordinary activity rather than for the purpose of measurement. Satellite imagery, card spending records, sensor readings, shipping manifests, mobile location pings and web scraping all fall under this heading. In practice, artificial intelligence is used to turn these raw and messy feeds into signals: computer vision counts cars in parking lots or tracks construction progress, models classify transactions into merchant categories, and language models parse shipping notices or scrape product listings at scale. The appeal is timing, because a satellite pass or a card swipe can register activity before a company reports it. The work is mostly pattern extraction and nowcasting, not prediction of prices or outcomes.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this field are mature. Satellite imagery analysis has become a standard input for tracking retail traffic, commodity inventories and industrial activity, and card transaction panels are widely used to estimate consumer spending. Sensor and shipping data are well established in logistics and trade monitoring, and web collection is routine for pricing and product assortment tracking. What is not solved is coverage and representativeness: card panels skew toward certain demographics, satellite revisits are limited by cloud and orbit, and location data has thinned after privacy changes. The honest limits are legal and ethical as much as technical, since scraping terms, consent for location data and material nonpublic information rules all constrain what can be used. Results also decay quickly, because once a signal is widely traded its edge narrows.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages here divide by data source and by the methods each one demands. Satellite Imagery covers overhead sensing and the computer vision pipelines that turn pixels into counts of activity. Card Transaction Data deals with spending records, merchant classification and the panel construction problems that shape consumer estimates. Sensor and Shipping Data covers industrial telemetry and vessel or freight tracking, where the signal is closer to physical throughput. Mobile Location Data addresses foot traffic and visitation patterns along with the privacy and consent questions that now define its limits. Web Data Collection covers scraping, crawling and parsing of public pages for prices, listings and disclosures. A reader would start with the page matching the data they can actually access, then move to the others to understand how signals from different sources are combined or checked against each other.
